source_metadata.title: Diagnosis Before Recovery: Turning Agent Failures into Selective Self-Correction

atoms.canonical_statement: The study evaluates whether diagnosing task-family failure modes before recovery can make language-agent self-correction more reliable and cost-aware than generic recovery playbooks.

DARC constructs a recovery harness in two stages: development-set failure diagnosis restricts admissible interventions, then training-set verifier feedback distills a frozen cost-aware fallback policy.
DARC assigns one dominant failure mode at the task-family level from development-set failure profiles and freezes that diagnosis before test evaluation.
The candidate recovery-intervention library is fixed before test evaluation; DARC restricts this pre-specified library rather than inventing new interventions at test time.
DARC uses training-set verifier outcomes to estimate intervention success and cost, while the reported protocol does not use test labels.
Candidate recovery policies are evaluated as short-circuit chains: interventions are tried in order and the chain stops when one succeeds.
The deployment objective trades empirical task success against recovery cost above a free-cost allowance using a penalty parameter lambda.
For the finite candidate spaces studied, the success component is a monotone submodular coverage objective over recovery interventions.

For a fixed finite chain class with bounded per-task cost, the paper gives a uniform-convergence argument in which reducing the admissible intervention set reduces the candidate policy class and finite-sample search risk.
ALFWorld is instantiated as an action-validity setting with recovery based on action pruning and admissibility guards.
AppWorld is instantiated as a procedure-breadth setting using Auto-Knowledge, local induction, and retrieval fallback interventions.
XBRL Finance is instantiated as a format-precision setting in which the admissible recovery interventions are retrieval few-shot demonstrations and retrieval-budget selection.
The main experiments compare DARC with Base LLM, ICL, MIPROv2, GEPA, and ACE; applicable offline-adaptation methods use the same training split and adaptation budget available to DARC.

For the headline AppWorld Test-Normal comparison, the analysis treats 56 scenarios (168 tasks) as independent clusters, uses 20,000 shared scenario-cluster bootstrap resamples for 95% confidence intervals, and applies paired tests with Holm correction.

population.label: AppWorld Test-Normal: 168 tasks nested in 56 scenarios

atoms.canonical_statement: AppWorld Test-Normal contains 168 tasks nested within 56 scenarios, with three tasks per scenario.
On ALFWorld valid_unseen with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DARC achieved 90.30% success versus 39.55% for the base agent and 54.48% for ACE.
On AppWorld Test-Normal with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DARC achieved 95.83% Task Goal Completion versus 23.21% for the base agent and 54.76% for ACE.
On AppWorld Test-Normal with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DARC achieved 87.50% Scenario Goal Completion versus 7.14% for the base agent and 39.29% for ACE.
On XBRL Finance with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DARC achieved 94.50% average accuracy versus 80.50% for ACE and 74.00% for MIPROv2.
DARC does not uniformly dominate every AppWorld challenge metric; ACE matches or exceeds DARC on some challenge metrics for Qwen3.5-27B and Qwen3.6-27B.
A Finance policy distilled on Formula and transferred to FiNER tags reached 89.50% accuracy versus 90.00% for the target-tuned DARC policy.
A Finance policy distilled on FiNER tags and transferred to Formula reached 96.00% accuracy versus 99.00% for the target-tuned DARC policy.
The ALFWorld action-validity policy frozen on valid_seen transferred to valid_unseen with 90.30% success.
In the diagnosis ablation, the correct ALFWorld recovery policy achieved 91.94% success versus 52.24% for both the generic and mismatched policies.
On AppWorld under the stricter diagnosis-ablation protocol, the correct recovery policy achieved 70.24% TGC versus 61.90% generic and 64.88% mismatched.
On AppWorld under the stricter diagnosis-ablation protocol, the correct recovery policy achieved 53.57% SGC versus 50.00% generic and 46.43% mismatched.
In the Finance diagnosis ablation, the correct recovery policy achieved 94.50% macro accuracy versus 80.50% generic and 37.75% mismatched.
On the 134-task ALFWorld valid_unseen fairness rerun, adding matched task metadata to the base agent increased success from 39.55% to 43.28%.
On the same ALFWorld rerun, restricting ACE to a random top-12 action view reduced success from 54.48% to 25.37%.
On the ALFWorld fairness rerun, DARC ranked recovery achieved 90.30% success with 0.575 invalid actions per episode.
On the ALFWorld fairness rerun, the DARC full guard achieved 89.55% success with 0.112 invalid actions per episode.
In the ALFWorld 2×2 factorial, the full action view without the recovery prompt solved 53 of 134 tasks (39.55%).

atoms.canonical_statement: In the ALFWorld 2×2 factorial, adding the recovery prompt to the full action view solved 52 of 134 tasks (38.81%).

concept.text: Full action view with recovery prompt

atoms.canonical_statement: In the ALFWorld 2×2 factorial, using the guard-ranked top-12 action view without the recovery prompt solved 58 of 134 tasks (43.28%).
In the ALFWorld 2×2 factorial, pairing the guard-ranked top-12 action view with the recovery prompt solved 119 of 134 tasks (88.81%).
The ALFWorld factorial difference-in-differences interaction for restricted action view × recovery prompt was reported as +46.27 percentage points.

atoms.canonical_statement: Forcing the action guard’s top-1 command at every step without a language model achieved 40.33% success on ALFWorld valid_unseen.

concept.text: Guard top-1 command without language model

atoms.canonical_statement: Applying the ranked view and recovery prompt to a plain base agent reached 82.28% success, leaving 6.53 percentage points attributed to the remaining harness components.

concept.text: Base agent + ranked view + recovery prompt

atoms.canonical_statement: In the preliminary Qwen3-8B weight-space extension, DARC-GRPO achieved 10.55% macro success, a +4.74 percentage-point gain over the 5.81% base.
In the preliminary Qwen3-8B weight-space extension, DARC-OPSD achieved 8.00% macro success, a +2.19 percentage-point gain over the 5.81% base.
The weight-space training extension is based on single-seed runs with modest absolute gains, and the authors treat it as a proof of concept rather than a verified training recipe.
The distilled Finance policy selected k=2 for Formula and k=1 for Tags, yielding 94.50% macro accuracy with a mean retrieval budget of 1.5 demonstrations.
Finance tag accuracy was non-monotonic with retrieval budget: fixed k=8 and k=16 slightly reduced tag accuracy relative to smaller budgets.
On ALFWorld with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DARC averaged 15.83 environment steps per episode versus 34.56 for the base agent.
On ALFWorld with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DARC averaged 0.091 invalid actions per episode versus 1.288 for the base agent.
On ALFWorld with DeepSeek-V4-Flash, DARC achieved 6.02 successes per 100 environment steps versus 1.16 for the base agent.

In the matched ALFWorld full-library-cascade control, the diagnosed cascade achieved 99.25% test success versus 98.51% for the full-library cascade; the reported +0.75 percentage-point difference had a 95% CI of 0.00 to 2.24 and was not significant.
The diagnosed ALFWorld cascade searched 40 candidate policies versus 400 for the full-library cascade.
Under resampling in the matched ALFWorld cascade control, the diagnosed cascade selected 14 distinct chains versus 34 for the full-library cascade.

concept.text: Distinct selected recovery chains under resampling

atoms.canonical_statement: On 72 development traces, the LLM automatic diagnosis achieved 97.22% agreement and Macro-F1 0.972 against a verifier-backed reference.
The evaluated system uses a static task-family-level diagnosis with one dominant failure mode per benchmark family; dynamic instance-level routing for mixed-mode failures is left to future work.

The offline evidence-matrix proxy assumes a controlled retry protocol in which later interventions are invoked only after earlier failures and success/cost can be attributed to the invoked intervention; resettable environments or evidence-only differences are used to support this assumption.
The structural coverage and finite-class arguments do not establish transfer across new failure modes; that remains an empirical question.
The AppWorld confidence intervals in the headline analysis quantify scenario-sampling uncertainty rather than variation across model-training seeds.
In the AppWorld diagnosis ablation, confidence intervals overlap despite a directional advantage for the correct policy.
The ALFWorld factorial decomposition is a single-run, temperature-0 analysis on one split and one backbone; corresponding factorial analyses for AppWorld and Finance are not available.

source_anchor.supplement: Appendix F / Scope of this decomposition

atoms.canonical_statement: The matched full-library recovery-cascade comparison that isolates diagnosis was reported for ALFWorld; extending this stronger baseline to the other task families remains future work.

The authors conclude that agent failures need not uniformly trigger more context: profiling failures to restrict admissible recovery interventions and distilling a cost-aware policy can turn self-correction into selective recovery-interface design.
